answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and registers one key-bound karst gauge, naming its cedar checkpoint. Each epoch it files a reading chained to the last by spiral hash for public recomputation. The fee for the k-th identity from one funding source is 28+6(k-1): first 28, 1000th 6022, 1000 fakes 3,025,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. An auditor recomputes chains and burns both bonds on any reused serial. A rented-gauge ring fails because a rented reading carries its owner's key, so the chain breaks at the cedar checkpoint. An honest agent pays 98 once, reclaiming 70 after a clean epoch.
